content.user_title: Process PDFs with Forms, Tables, and OCR
content.value_statement: PDF workflows often need reliable extraction, validation, and batch processing. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical PDF workflows for forms, tables, OCR, and checks.
actual_capabilities: Extract PDF form field metadata with scripts/analyze_form.py.
Explain form filling, validation, flattening, and multi-page field handling.
Describe table extraction methods and exports to CSV, Excel, and JSON.
Describe OCR setup, image preprocessing, language selection, and text export.
Show batch processing, exit codes, logging, and error-handling patterns.
limitations: Only scripts/analyze_form.py is present in this package.
Other script names are documented examples and may require user implementation.
OCR needs Tesseract and related Python packages installed.
Extraction accuracy depends on PDF structure, scan quality, and form format.

use_cases.title: Automate Form Intake
use_cases.description: Operations teams can inspect form fields, validate submissions, and plan filled PDF outputs.

use_cases.title: Extract Report Tables
use_cases.description: Data analysts can plan table extraction and export results for spreadsheet review.

use_cases.title: Process Scanned Documents
use_cases.description: Records teams can design OCR workflows with preprocessing and language selection.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PDF Processing Pro to inspect this PDF form. List fields, required inputs, field types, and validation concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PDF Processing Pro to plan table extraction from this report. Recommend settings, output format, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build OCR Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PDF Processing Pro to design an OCR workflow for scanned PDFs. Include preprocessing, language settings, quality checks, and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Design Batch Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PDF Processing Pro to design a batch pipeline for many PDFs. Include validation, error handling, logging, retries, and output organization.

output_examples.input: A tax form template that needs field mapping before automation.
output_examples.output: A field inventory with required fields, field types, suggested validation rules, and output planning notes.

output_examples.input: A monthly sales report with tables across several pages.
output_examples.output: A table extraction plan with export format guidance, validation checks, and post-processing steps.

output_examples.input: A scanned application packet with mixed English and Spanish text.
output_examples.output: An OCR workflow with preprocessing steps, language settings, confidence review, and text export guidance.

best_practices: Validate inputs and output paths before processing any PDF.
Test each workflow with representative sample documents first.
Review extracted text and tables before using them in decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not run elevated installation commands from an agent without user approval.
Do not overwrite original PDFs without a verified backup.
Do not treat OCR or table extraction output as final without review.

faq.question: Can this skill fill PDF forms?
faq.answer: It explains form filling patterns and includes a form analysis script. Some referenced fill scripts are examples, not included files.

faq.question: Does it support scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. The OCR guide covers Tesseract, image preprocessing, language selection, and text export.

faq.question: Can it extract tables?
faq.answer: Yes. The table guide explains extraction strategies and exports to CSV, Excel, and JSON.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require system packages?
faq.answer: OCR workflows require Tesseract. Elevated installation commands should be handled manually by the user.

faq.question: Is it ready for production?
faq.answer: It provides production-oriented patterns, but teams should add path validation, tests, and review steps before deployment.
